root_cause.mechanism: The replacement of `pkgutil.get_loader(name)` with `importlib.util.find_spec(name)` introduced a regression because `find_spec` raises `ValueError` if the module exists in `sys.modules` but has its `__spec__` attribute set to `None`. This happens for the `__main__` module when running a script directly. The previous `pkgutil.get_loader` implementation handled this gracefully.

limitations: The test suite has some pre-existing failures in `tests/test_cli.py` due to an apparent incompatibility with the installed version of `click` (CliRunner does not accept `mix_stderr`). These failures are unrelated to the reported bug and my fix.

hypotheses.text: Commit 84e11a1e replaced pkgutil.get_loader with importlib.util.find_spec without handling ValueError (such as when sys.modules[name].__spec__ is None or invalid name), causing unhandled exceptions in get_root_path and _find_package_path.
hypotheses.predicts: Catching (ImportError, ValueError) around importlib.util.find_spec in helpers.py and scaffold.py (where pkgutil.get_loader was replaced) will allow find_spec to gracefully return None/catch the error, making Flask("__main__") and direct script execution succeed.
hypotheses.evidence: find_spec raises ValueError when a module exists in sys.modules but has __spec__=None. This is the case for __main__ when run as a script. The previous code used pkgutil.get_loader which didn't have this behavior.

hypotheses.text: The bug is caused specifically by __main__ missing __spec__ when run as a script, so find_spec should only be avoided when import_name == '__main__'.
hypotheses.predicts: Bypassing find_spec exclusively when root_mod_name == '__main__' is sufficient and other modules never trigger find_spec failure in sys.modules.
hypotheses.evidence: Any module in sys.modules with __spec__=None will trigger this, not just __main__.
